election.permnull_conc_gt1_mean.spec: MEAN count of cells (the single most pivotal period contributes more than the champion's whole net margin) under the within-period model-label permutation null, 2000 draws, seed 20260902. The null permutes model labels within each period independently, preserving each period's own multiset of losses (so its difficulty and dispersion, including the 2020 cliff at full size) and every marginal loss value -- destroying the association between model identity and performance, and with it each named model's serial persistence across periods and the correlation between named models' loss series (the real panel's median cross-model level correlation is recorded as modelset.loss_corr_median; the permuted counterpart is not measured by this producer). Compare against the observed count in the `observed` field: this is the arbitrary-winner benchmark Section 5's own language implicitly claims to beat.

election.permnull_conc_gt1_p_ge.spec: P(null count >= observed) for the single most pivotal period contributes more than the champion's whole net margin. A LARGE value means the observed count is at or BELOW what an arbitrary winner produces -- i.e. the raw count is not evidence of the aggregation fragility Section 5 describes.

election.permnull_conc_gt1_p_le.spec: P(null count <= observed) for the single most pivotal period contributes more than the champion's whole net margin. A SMALL value means the observed count is significantly BELOW the null -- a finding in the OPPOSITE direction from the one the raw count suggests.

NOT EVIDENCE OF FRAGILITY ON ITS OWN, and must not be reported as such: the exchangeable null's own median sits well BELOW 0.60 (it is 0.504 -- see election.stability_null_median), so a 0.60 cut sits ABOVE the arbitrary-winner benchmark and would flag most of a pure-null panel. Only cells below the null's 5th percentile (election.stability_null_p05) are unusually fragile relative to chance; that count is election.stability_below_null_p05, reported with its own expected value
